import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures

The Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures relate the values at `1` of the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of a
finite Weyl group `W` to the representation theory of the corresponding complex semisimple Lie
algebra `𝔤`.

Let `𝔥 ⊆ 𝔤` be a Cartan subalgebra, fix a base (system of simple roots) of the root system, let
`ρ` be the half-sum of the positive roots and let `W` be the Weyl group. For `w ∈ W` let `M_w` be
the Verma module of highest weight `-w(ρ) - ρ` and let `L_w` be its unique simple quotient. Write
`ch` for the formal character, `≤` for the Bruhat order, `ℓ` for the Coxeter length and `w₀` for
the longest element of `W`. The two (equivalent) conjectures state that for all `w ∈ W`
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) =
  \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1) \operatorname{ch}(M_y)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y).$$

Both were proved in 1981 by Beilinson–Bernstein and, independently, by Brylinski–Kashiwara.

## Formalisation notes

* A complex semisimple Lie algebra is a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra with non-degenerate
  Killing form (`LieAlgebra.IsKilling ℂ L`). Its Weyl group is `(rootSystem H).weylGroup`.
* Mathlib has neither Hecke algebras nor Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Following Björner–Brenti,
  *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, Section 5.1, the `R`-polynomials are characterised by the
  Kazhdan–Lusztig recursion, and the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials by the identity
  $q^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(q^{-1}) = \sum_{y \le a \le w} R_{y,a}(q) P_{a,w}(q)$ together
  with the degree bound $\deg P_{y,w} \le (\ell(w) - \ell(y) - 1)/2$ for $y < w$. Both
  characterisations determine the families uniquely (and the families exist), so the conjectures
  are stated for the family `P` satisfying `IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials`.
* The Verma module `M(λ)` is `U(𝔤)/I(λ)`, where `I(λ)` is the left ideal generated by the
  positive root spaces and by `h - λ(h)` for `h ∈ 𝔥`; `L(λ)` is its quotient by the sum of all
  proper submodules. Equality of formal characters is stated as equality of all weight
  multiplicities.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_polynomial%23Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_conjectures)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D. Kazhdan, G. Lusztig, *Representations of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras*,
  Invent. Math. 53 (1979), 165–184.
- A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein, *Localisation de 𝔤-modules*, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 292 (1981).
- J.-L. Brylinski, M. Kashiwara, *Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture and holonomic systems*,
  Invent. Math. 64 (1981), 387–410.
- A. Björner, F. Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, Springer GTM 231 (2005), Section 5.1.
- J. E. Humphreys, *Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras in the BGG Category 𝒪*,
  AMS GSM 94 (2008), Chapters 1 and 8.
-/

namespace KazhdanLusztigConjectures

open LieAlgebra LieModule Module Polynomial

/- Coxeter combinatorics of the Weyl group of a root pairing with a base. -/

section WeylGroup

variable {ι R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N]
  [Module R N] {P : RootPairing ι R M N} (b : P.Base)

/-- The simple reflections `s_i` (`i` a simple root of the base `b`) as elements of the Weyl
group. -/
def simpleReflections : Set P.weylGroup :=
  {s | ∃ i ∈ b.support, s = RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i}

/-- The Coxeter length `ℓ(w)`: the smallest number of simple reflections whose product is `w`. -/
noncomputable def length (w : P.weylGroup) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ l : List P.weylGroup,
    (∀ s ∈ l, s ∈ simpleReflections b) ∧ l.length = n ∧ l.prod = w}

/-- The reflections of the Weyl group: the conjugates of the simple reflections. -/
def IsReflection (t : P.weylGroup) : Prop :=
  ∃ w, ∃ s ∈ simpleReflections b, t = w * s * w⁻¹

/-- The (strong) Bruhat order `x ≤ w` on the Weyl group: the reflexive-transitive closure of the
relation `x → x * t`, where `t` is a reflection with `ℓ(x) < ℓ(x * t)`. -/
def BruhatLE : P.weylGroup → P.weylGroup → Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen fun x y => ∃ t, IsReflection b t ∧ y = x * t ∧ length b x < length b y

/-- `R` is the family of `R`-polynomials `R_{x,y} ∈ ℤ[q]` of the Weyl group. It is characterised
(see Björner–Brenti, Section 5.1) by: `R_{x,y} = 0` unless `x ≤ y`, `R_{x,x} = 1`, and for every
simple reflection `s` with `sy < y`: `R_{x,y} = R_{sx,sy}` if `sx < x`, and
`R_{x,y} = (q - 1) R_{sx,y} + q R_{sx,sy}` if `sx > x`. -/
structure IsRPolynomials (R : P.weylGroup → P.weylGroup → ℤ[X]) : Prop where
  eq_zero_of_not_le : ∀ x y, ¬ BruhatLE b x y → R x y = 0
  self : ∀ x, R x x = 1
  eq_of_lt_of_lt : ∀ s ∈ simpleReflections b, ∀ x y, length b (s * y) < length b y →
    length b (s * x) < length b x → R x y = R (s * x) (s * y)
  eq_of_lt_of_gt : ∀ s ∈ simpleReflections b, ∀ x y, length b (s * y) < length b y →
    length b x < length b (s * x) → R x y = (X - 1) * R (s * x) y + X * R (s * x) (s * y)

/-- `Q` is the family of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials `P_{x,y} ∈ ℤ[q]` of the Weyl group. It is
characterised (see Björner–Brenti, Theorem 5.1.4) by: `P_{x,y} = 0` unless `x ≤ y`,
`P_{x,x} = 1`, `deg P_{x,y} ≤ (ℓ(y) - ℓ(x) - 1) / 2` for `x < y`, and
$q^{\ell(y) - \ell(x)} P_{x,y}(q^{-1}) = \sum_{x \le a \le y} R_{x,a}(q) P_{a,y}(q)$ for `x ≤ y`,
where `R` is the family of `R`-polynomials. -/
structure IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials (Q : P.weylGroup → P.weylGroup → ℤ[X]) : Prop where
  eq_zero_of_not_le : ∀ x y, ¬ BruhatLE b x y → Q x y = 0
  self : ∀ x, Q x x = 1
  natDegree_le : ∀ x y, BruhatLE b x y → x ≠ y →
    2 * (Q x y).natDegree + 1 + length b x ≤ length b y
  reflect_eq : ∃ R, IsRPolynomials b R ∧ ∀ x y, BruhatLE b x y →
    (Q x y).reflect (length b y - length b x) =
      ∑ᶠ (a) (_ : BruhatLE b x a ∧ BruhatLE b a y), R x a * Q a y

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem bruhatLE_refl (w : P.weylGroup) : BruhatLE b w w :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem length_one : length b 1 = 0 :=
  Nat.sInf_eq_zero.mpr <| Or.inl ⟨[], by simp, rfl, rfl⟩

end WeylGroup

/- Verma modules and simple highest weight modules of a complex semisimple Lie algebra. -/

section LieAlgebra

variable {L : Type*} [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]
  (H : LieSubalgebra ℂ L) [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] (b : (IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base)

local notation "𝔘" => UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra ℂ L

/-- The nilpotent subalgebra `𝔫⁺ = ⨁_{α > 0} 𝔤_α` spanned by the positive root spaces. -/
noncomputable def positiveRootSpaces : Submodule ℂ L :=
  ⨆ α : H.root, ⨆ (_ : b.IsPos α), (rootSpace H (α : H → ℂ)).toSubmodule

/-- The left ideal `I(λ)` of `U(𝔤)` generated by `𝔫⁺` and by `h - λ(h)` for `h ∈ 𝔥`. -/
noncomputable def vermaIdeal (μ : Dual ℂ H) : Submodule 𝔘 𝔘 :=
  Submodule.span 𝔘
    ((UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ '' (positiveRootSpaces H b : Set L)) ∪
      Set.range fun h : H => UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ (h : L) - algebraMap ℂ 𝔘 (μ h))

/-- The Verma module `M(λ) = U(𝔤) / I(λ)` of highest weight `λ`. -/
abbrev VermaModule (μ : Dual ℂ H) := 𝔘 ⧸ vermaIdeal H b μ

noncomputable instance (μ : Dual ℂ H) : LieRingModule L (VermaModule H b μ) :=
  letI : LieRingModule 𝔘 (VermaModule H b μ) := LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule
  LieRingModule.compLieHom _ (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ)

instance (μ : Dual ℂ H) : LieModule ℂ L (VermaModule H b μ) :=
  letI : LieRingModule 𝔘 (VermaModule H b μ) := LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule
  haveI : LieModule ℂ 𝔘 (VermaModule H b μ) := LieModule.ofAssociativeModule
  LieModule.compLieHom _ (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ)

/-- The unique maximal proper submodule `N(λ)` of the Verma module `M(λ)`: the sum of all its
proper submodules. -/
noncomputable def maximalSubmodule (μ : Dual ℂ H) : LieSubmodule ℂ L (VermaModule H b μ) :=
  sSup {N | N ≠ ⊤}

/-- The simple highest weight module `L(λ) = M(λ) / N(λ)`. -/
abbrev SimpleHighestWeightModule (μ : Dual ℂ H) := VermaModule H b μ ⧸ maximalSubmodule H b μ

/-- The formal character of a `𝔤`-module `X`, i.e. the weight multiplicity `dim X_μ` at
`μ ∈ 𝔥*`. -/
noncomputable def character (X : Type*) [AddCommGroup X] [Module ℂ X] [LieRingModule L X]
    [LieModule ℂ L X] (μ : Dual ℂ H) : ℤ :=
  finrank ℂ (weightSpace X (μ : H → ℂ))

/-- The Weyl vector `ρ`: the half-sum of the positive roots. -/
noncomputable def weylVector : Dual ℂ H :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ∑ α ∈ Finset.univ.filter b.IsPos, (IsKilling.rootSystem H).root α

local notation "W" => RootPairing.weylGroup (IsKilling.rootSystem H)

/-- The Verma module `M_w` of highest weight `-w(ρ) - ρ`. -/
abbrev vermaModuleOf (w : W) := VermaModule H b (-(w • weylVector H b) - weylVector H b)

/-- The simple module `L_w` of highest weight `-w(ρ) - ρ`. -/
abbrev simpleModuleOf (w : W) :=
  SimpleHighestWeightModule H b (-(w • weylVector H b) - weylVector H b)

/-- **First Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and
by Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981).

Let `𝔤` be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra `𝔥`, a fixed base of the root
system, Weyl vector `ρ` and Weyl group `W`. For `w ∈ W` let `M_w` be the Verma module of highest
weight `-w(ρ) - ρ` and `L_w` its simple quotient. Then, for every `w ∈ W`,
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) =
  \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1) \operatorname{ch}(M_y),$$
where `≤` is the Bruhat order, `ℓ` the Coxeter length and `P_{y,w}` the Kazhdan–Lusztig
polynomials of `W`. The equality of formal characters is stated as the equality of the weight
multiplicities at every `μ ∈ 𝔥*`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20 22]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i (P : W → W → ℤ[X])
    (hP : IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials b P) (w : W) (μ : Dual ℂ H) :
    character H (simpleModuleOf H b w) μ =
      ∑ᶠ (y) (_ : BruhatLE b y w),
        (-1) ^ (length b w - length b y) * (P y w).eval 1 *
          character H (vermaModuleOf H b y) μ := by
  sorry

/-- **Second Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and
by Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981), equivalent to the first one.

With the notation of `kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i`, and `w₀` the element of maximal
length of `W`, for every `w ∈ W`
$$\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y),$$
i.e. the multiplicity of `L_y` in `M_w` is `P_{w₀w, w₀y}(1)`. The equality of formal characters
is stated as the equality of the weight multiplicities at every `μ ∈ 𝔥*`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20 22]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.ii (P : W → W → ℤ[X])
    (hP : IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials b P) (w₀ : W) (hw₀ : ∀ y, length b y ≤ length b w₀)
    (w : W) (μ : Dual ℂ H) :
    character H (vermaModuleOf H b w) μ =
      ∑ᶠ (y) (_ : BruhatLE b y w),
        (P (w₀ * w) (w₀ * y)).eval 1 * character H (simpleModuleOf H b y) μ := by
  sorry

end LieAlgebra

end KazhdanLusztigConjectures

Mathlib has no Coxeter-system structure on the Weyl group, no Bruhat order, no Hecke algebra and no Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are not constructed but characterised: `IsRPolynomials` is the Wikipedia/Björner–Brenti recursion for R-polynomials (R_{x,y}=0 unless x≤y, R_{x,x}=1, and for simple s with sy<y: R_{x,y}=R_{sx,sy} if sx<x, R_{x,y}=(q−1)R_{sx,y}+qR_{sx,sy} if sx>x); `IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials` is Björner–Brenti Thm 5.1.4 (P_{x,y}=0 unless x≤y, P_{x,x}=1, 2·deg P_{x,y}+1 ≤ ℓ(y)−ℓ(x) for x<y, and q^{ℓ(y)−ℓ(x)}P_{x,y}(q⁻¹) = Σ_{x≤a≤y} R_{x,a}P_{a,y}, encoded with `Polynomial.reflect`). Both specs determine the families uniquely and are satisfied by the genuine polynomials, so quantifying `∀ P, IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials b P → …` is equivalent to the conjecture. A reviewer should confirm the two specs against the sources (the arXiv:1211.4305 background paper restates both verbatim).

Verma module M(λ) := U(𝔤)/I(λ) with I(λ) the left ideal (`Submodule 𝔘 𝔘` span) generated by the positive root spaces and by ι(h) − λ(h)·1, h ∈ 𝔥 (Humphreys, Category O, §1.3); the 𝔤-module structure is via `UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι` (checked: ⁅h, [m]⁆ = [ι(h)·m] by rfl). L(λ) := M(λ)/N(λ) with N(λ) = `sSup {N | N ≠ ⊤}`, the sum of all proper submodules, which is the unique maximal submodule.

Formal characters are compared through weight multiplicities: `character H X μ := finrank ℂ (weightSpace X μ)` (ℤ-valued), and each conjecture is stated for every μ ∈ 𝔥*. Weight spaces are simultaneous eigenspaces (`weightSpace`, not `genWeightSpace`), which agree for Verma modules and their quotients where 𝔥 acts semisimply; weight spaces of these modules are finite-dimensional so `finrank` is honest.
Sums over {y | y ≤ w} (and Bruhat intervals in the KL spec) use `finsum` because Mathlib has no `Finite` instance for the Weyl group; W is finite, so these are the actual finite sums.
The sign (−1)^{ℓ(w)−ℓ(y)} uses ℕ-subtraction, valid since `BruhatLE b y w` implies ℓ(y) ≤ ℓ(w) by construction.

/-- **First Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and
by Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981).

Let `𝔤` be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra `𝔥`, a fixed base of the root
system, Weyl vector `ρ` and Weyl group `W`. For `w ∈ W` let `M_w` be the Verma module of highest
weight `-w(ρ) - ρ` and `L_w` its simple quotient. Then, for every `w ∈ W`,
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) =
  \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1) \operatorname{ch}(M_y),$$
where `≤` is the Bruhat order, `ℓ` the Coxeter length and `P_{y,w}` the Kazhdan–Lusztig
polynomials of `W`. The equality of formal characters is stated as the equality of the weight
multiplicities at every `μ ∈ 𝔥*`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20 22]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i (P : W → W → ℤ[X])
    (hP : IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials b P) (w : W) (μ : Dual ℂ H) :
    character H (simpleModuleOf H b w) μ =
      ∑ᶠ (y) (_ : BruhatLE b y w),
        (-1) ^ (length b w - length b y) * (P y w).eval 1 *
          character H (vermaModuleOf H b y) μ := by
  sorry

With the notation of `kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i`, and `w₀` the element of maximal

$$\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y),$$
i.e. the multiplicity of `L_y` in `M_w` is `P_{w₀w, w₀y}(1)`. The equality of formal characters
is stated as the equality of the weight multiplicities at every `μ ∈ 𝔥*`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20 22]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.ii (P : W → W → ℤ[X])

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures

The Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures relate the values at $q = 1$ of the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
$P_{y,w}$ of a finite Weyl group $W$ to the representation theory of the corresponding complex
semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$.

Let $\mathfrak{h} \subseteq \mathfrak{g}$ be a Cartan subalgebra, fix a base of the root system
(equivalently, a system of positive roots), and let $\rho$ be the half-sum of the positive roots.
For $w \in W$ let $M_w$ be the Verma module of highest weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$ and let $L_w$ be
its unique simple quotient. Writing $\operatorname{ch}$ for the formal character, the conjectures
state that for all $w \in W$
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) =
  \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1) \operatorname{ch}(M_y)$$
and
$$\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y),$$
where $\le$ is the Bruhat order, $\ell$ is the Coxeter length and $w_0$ is the longest element
of $W$. Both were proved in 1981 by Beilinson–Bernstein and by Brylinski–Kashiwara.

Mathlib does not contain Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, the Bruhat order or Verma modules. This
file defines the Bruhat order and characterises the $R$-polynomials and the Kazhdan–Lusztig
polynomials by the standard axioms (Björner–Brenti, Theorems 5.1.1 and 5.1.4), which determine
them uniquely; the conjectures are then stated for any family of polynomials satisfying these
axioms. Verma modules are constructed as quotients of the universal enveloping algebra.

A complex semisimple Lie algebra is modelled as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $\mathbb{C}$
with non-degenerate Killing form (`LieAlgebra.IsKilling`); by Cartan's criterion this is
equivalent to semisimplicity. The Weyl group is `RootPairing.weylGroup` of the root system of
$\mathfrak{g}$. Mathlib does not yet know that it is finite, nor that it is a Coxeter group with
respect to the simple reflections, so both facts are taken as hypotheses.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_polynomial%23Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_conjectures)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D. Kazhdan, G. Lusztig, *Representations of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras*,
  Invent. Math. 53 (1979), 165–184.
- A. Björner, F. Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, GTM 231, Springer, 2005, Chapter 5.
- J. E. Humphreys, *Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras in the BGG Category $\mathcal{O}$*,
  GSM 94, AMS, 2008, Sections 1.3 and 8.4.
-/

namespace KazhdanLusztigConjectures

open Polynomial

section Coxeter

variable {B W : Type*} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W)

local prefix:100 "s" => cs.simple
local prefix:100 "ℓ" => cs.length

/-- The Bruhat order on a Coxeter group: `u ≤ v` if there is a chain
`u = x₀ → x₁ → ⋯ → xₖ = v` where each step is `xⱼ → xⱼ t` for a reflection `t`
with `ℓ(xⱼ) < ℓ(xⱼ t)` (Björner–Brenti, Definition 2.1.1). -/
def BruhatLE (u v : W) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun x y => ∃ t, cs.IsReflection t ∧ y = x * t ∧ ℓ x < ℓ y) u v

local infix:50 " ≤ᴮ " => BruhatLE cs

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem bruhatLE_refl (w : W) : w ≤ᴮ w :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem bruhatLE_trans {u v w : W} (h₁ : u ≤ᴮ v) (h₂ : v ≤ᴮ w) : u ≤ᴮ w :=
  h₁.trans h₂

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem length_le_of_bruhatLE {u v : W} (h : u ≤ᴮ v) : ℓ u ≤ ℓ v := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact le_rfl
  | tail _ h ih => exact ih.trans h.choose_spec.2.2.le

/-- `IsRPolynomials cs R` says that `R : W → W → ℤ[X]` is the family of $R$-polynomials
$R_{u,v}(q)$ of the Coxeter system `cs`. These are the polynomials with
* $R_{u,v} = 0$ unless $u \le v$ in the Bruhat order,
* $R_{v,v} = 1$,
* for a right descent $s$ of $v$: $R_{u,v} = R_{us,vs}$ if $s$ is a right descent of $u$, and
  $R_{u,v} = (q - 1) R_{u,vs} + q R_{us,vs}$ otherwise.

These conditions determine the family uniquely (Björner–Brenti, Theorem 5.1.1). -/
structure IsRPolynomials (R : W → W → ℤ[X]) : Prop where
  eq_zero_of_not_bruhatLE (u v : W) : ¬ u ≤ᴮ v → R u v = 0
  self (v : W) : R v v = 1
  of_isRightDescent (u v : W) (i : B) : cs.IsRightDescent v i → cs.IsRightDescent u i →
    R u v = R (u * s i) (v * s i)
  of_not_isRightDescent (u v : W) (i : B) : cs.IsRightDescent v i → ¬ cs.IsRightDescent u i →
    R u v = (X - 1) * R u (v * s i) + X * R (u * s i) (v * s i)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem eq_one_of_bruhatLE_one {u : W} (h : u ≤ᴮ 1) : u = 1 :=
  cs.length_eq_zero_iff.mp <| Nat.le_zero.mp <|
    (length_le_of_bruhatLE cs h).trans_eq cs.length_one

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsRPolynomials.eq_zero_of_ne_one {R : W → W → ℤ[X]} (hR : IsRPolynomials cs R) {u : W}
    (hu : u ≠ 1) : R u 1 = 0 :=
  hR.eq_zero_of_not_bruhatLE u 1 fun h => hu (eq_one_of_bruhatLE_one cs h)

variable [Fintype W]

open scoped Classical in
/-- `IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials cs R P` says that `P : W → W → ℤ[X]` is the family of
Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials $P_{u,v}(q)$ of the finite Coxeter system `cs`, given that `R` is
the family of $R$-polynomials. These are the polynomials with
* $P_{u,v} = 0$ unless $u \le v$ in the Bruhat order,
* $P_{v,v} = 1$,
* $\deg P_{u,v} \le (\ell(v) - \ell(u) - 1)/2$ for $u < v$,
* $q^{\ell(v) - \ell(u)} P_{u,v}(q^{-1}) = \sum_{u \le a \le v} R_{u,a}(q) P_{a,v}(q)$ for
  $u \le v$.

These conditions determine the family uniquely (Björner–Brenti, Theorem 5.1.4). The left hand
side of the last condition is expressed with `Polynomial.reflect n p`, which is $q^n p(q^{-1})$
whenever $\deg p \le n$. -/
structure IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials (R P : W → W → ℤ[X]) : Prop where
  eq_zero_of_not_bruhatLE (u v : W) : ¬ u ≤ᴮ v → P u v = 0
  self (v : W) : P v v = 1
  degree_le (u v : W) : u ≤ᴮ v → u ≠ v →
    (P u v).degree ≤ ((ℓ v - ℓ u - 1) / 2 : ℕ)
  reflect_eq (u v : W) : u ≤ᴮ v →
    (P u v).reflect (ℓ v - ℓ u) =
      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => u ≤ᴮ a ∧ a ≤ᴮ v), R u a * P a v

end Coxeter

section LieAlgebra

open LieAlgebra LieModule Module

variable {L : Type*} [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]
  {H : LieSubalgebra ℂ L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra]

local notation "Φ" => IsKilling.rootSystem H
local notation "𝔚" => RootPairing.weylGroup Φ

variable (b : RootPairing.Base (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H))

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Weyl vector $\rho$: half the sum of the positive roots (positive with respect to the
base `b`). -/
noncomputable def weylVector : Dual ℂ H :=
  (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • ∑ α : H.root with b.IsPos α, RootPairing.root Φ α

/-- The nilpotent subalgebra $\mathfrak{n}^+ = \bigoplus_{\alpha > 0} \mathfrak{g}_\alpha$
spanned by the root spaces of the positive roots, as a subspace of the Lie algebra. -/
noncomputable def positiveNilradical : Submodule ℂ L :=
  ⨆ α : H.root, ⨆ (_ : b.IsPos α), (rootSpace H (α : H → ℂ)).toSubmodule

local notation "𝒰" => UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra ℂ L

/-- The left ideal $I_\lambda$ of the universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{g})$ generated by
$\mathfrak{n}^+$ and by the elements $h - \lambda(h) \cdot 1$ for $h \in \mathfrak{h}$. -/
noncomputable def vermaIdeal (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Submodule 𝒰 𝒰 :=
  Submodule.span 𝒰
    (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ '' (positiveNilradical b : Set L) ∪
      Set.range fun h : H => UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ (h : L) - algebraMap ℂ 𝒰 (χ h))

/-- The Verma module $M(\lambda) = U(\mathfrak{g}) / I_\lambda$ of highest weight $\lambda$.
It is isomorphic to $U(\mathfrak{g}) \otimes_{U(\mathfrak{b})} \mathbb{C}_\lambda$
(Humphreys, Section 1.3). -/
abbrev VermaModule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Type _ :=
  𝒰 ⧸ vermaIdeal b χ

/-- The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ acts on $M(\lambda)$ through $U(\mathfrak{g})$. -/
noncomputable instance (χ : Dual ℂ H) : LieRingModule L (VermaModule b χ) :=
  letI : LieRingModule 𝒰 (VermaModule b χ) := LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule
  LieRingModule.compLieHom (VermaModule b χ) (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ)

noncomputable instance (χ : Dual ℂ H) : LieModule ℂ L (VermaModule b χ) :=
  letI : LieRingModule 𝒰 (VermaModule b χ) := LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule
  haveI : LieModule ℂ 𝒰 (VermaModule b χ) := LieModule.ofAssociativeModule
  LieModule.compLieHom (VermaModule b χ) (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℂ)

/-- The unique maximal proper submodule $N(\lambda)$ of the Verma module $M(\lambda)$, defined as
the sum of all proper submodules. -/
noncomputable def vermaMaximalSubmodule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : LieSubmodule ℂ L (VermaModule b χ) :=
  sSup {N | N ≠ ⊤}

/-- The simple highest weight module $L(\lambda) = M(\lambda) / N(\lambda)$ of highest weight
$\lambda$: the unique simple quotient of the Verma module $M(\lambda)$. -/
abbrev SimpleHighestWeightModule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Type _ :=
  VermaModule b χ ⧸ vermaMaximalSubmodule b χ

variable (H) in
/-- The formal character of a $\mathfrak{g}$-module $X$: the function
$\mu \mapsto \dim X_\mu$ recording the dimensions of the weight spaces
$X_\mu = \{x \in X \mid h \cdot x = \mu(h) x \text{ for all } h \in \mathfrak{h}\}$,
i.e. the formal sum $\operatorname{ch}(X) = \sum_\mu \dim X_\mu \, e^\mu$. -/
noncomputable def formalCharacter (X : Type*) [AddCommGroup X] [Module ℂ X] [LieRingModule L X]
    [LieModule ℂ L X] : Dual ℂ H → ℤ :=
  fun μ => finrank ℂ (weightSpace X (μ : H → ℂ))

end LieAlgebra

section Conjectures

open LieAlgebra Module

variable {L : Type*} [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]
  {H : LieSubalgebra ℂ L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra]

local notation "Φ" => IsKilling.rootSystem H
local notation "𝔚" => RootPairing.weylGroup Φ

open scoped Classical in
/--
**First Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and
Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981).

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}$,
Weyl group $W$ and a fixed base (system of positive roots), and let $\rho$ be the half-sum of the
positive roots. Regard $W$ as a Coxeter group with respect to the simple reflections. For
$w \in W$ let $M_w$ be the Verma module of highest weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$ and $L_w$ its simple
quotient. Then for every $w \in W$
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) =
  \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1) \operatorname{ch}(M_y),$$
where $\le$ is the Bruhat order, $\ell$ the Coxeter length and $P_{y,w}$ the Kazhdan–Lusztig
polynomials of $W$.

Here `cs` is any Coxeter system on the Weyl group whose simple generators are the simple
reflections, and `R`, `P` are the (uniquely determined) families of $R$-polynomials and
Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of `cs`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i (b : RootPairing.Base Φ) [Fintype 𝔚]
    {cm : CoxeterMatrix b.support} (cs : CoxeterSystem cm 𝔚)
    (hcs : ∀ i : b.support, cs.simple i = RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx Φ i)
    (R P : 𝔚 → 𝔚 → ℤ[X])
    (hR : IsRPolynomials cs R) (hP : IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials cs R P) (w : 𝔚) :
    formalCharacter H (SimpleHighestWeightModule b (-(w • weylVector b) - weylVector b)) =
      ∑ y ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun y => BruhatLE cs y w),
        ((-1) ^ (cs.length w - cs.length y) * (P y w).eval 1) •
          formalCharacter H (VermaModule b (-(y • weylVector b) - weylVector b)) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
**Second Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and
Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981). It is equivalent to the first conjecture.

With notation as in the first conjecture, for every $w \in W$
$$\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y),$$
where $w_0$ is the element of maximal length of $W$. Equivalently, the multiplicity of $L_y$ in
$M_w$ is $[M_w : L_y] = P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1)$.

Here `cs` is any Coxeter system on the Weyl group whose simple generators are the simple
reflections, `R`, `P` are the (uniquely determined) families of $R$-polynomials and
Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of `cs`, and `w₀` is any element of maximal length (there is exactly
one). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.ii (b : RootPairing.Base Φ) [Fintype 𝔚]
    {cm : CoxeterMatrix b.support} (cs : CoxeterSystem cm 𝔚)
    (hcs : ∀ i : b.support, cs.simple i = RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx Φ i)
    (R P : 𝔚 → 𝔚 → ℤ[X])
    (hR : IsRPolynomials cs R) (hP : IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials cs R P)
    (w₀ : 𝔚) (hw₀ : ∀ w, cs.length w ≤ cs.length w₀) (w : 𝔚) :
    formalCharacter H (VermaModule b (-(w • weylVector b) - weylVector b)) =
      ∑ y ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun y => BruhatLE cs y w),
        (P (w₀ * w) (w₀ * y)).eval 1 •
          formalCharacter H
            (SimpleHighestWeightModule b (-(y • weylVector b) - weylVector b)) := by
  sorry

end Conjectures

end KazhdanLusztigConjectures
attempts.decomposition_objections: No objection to the two-part decomposition; it matches the article exactly. One note: the problem header says "Status: open" while the table notes (correctly) say the conjectures were proved in 1981 and should be `research solved`; I followed the notes and CONTRIBUTING.md and tagged both slots `research solved`.
modeling_decisions: Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and R-polynomials are not constructed; they are characterised by predicates `IsRPolynomials` (Björner–Brenti Thm 5.1.1: R_{u,v}=0 unless u≤v, R_{v,v}=1, right-descent recursion R_{u,v}=R_{us,vs} if s∈D_R(u), (q−1)R_{u,vs}+qR_{us,vs} otherwise) and `IsKazhdanLusztigPolynomials` (Thm 5.1.4: P_{u,v}=0 unless u≤v, P_{v,v}=1, deg P_{u,v} ≤ (ℓ(v)−ℓ(u)−1)/2 for u<v, q^{ℓ(v)−ℓ(u)}P_{u,v}(q⁻¹)=Σ_{u≤a≤v}R_{u,a}P_{a,v}). Each theorem quantifies over all (R,P) satisfying these axioms; since exactly one such family exists (a theorem), this is equivalent to the original statement. Reviewer should check the axiom transcription; the last axiom was independently re-derived from the Hecke-algebra definition (D-invariance of C'_w) in the article, and the right-descent R-recursion was checked to agree with the article's left version.

q^{ℓ(v)−ℓ(u)} P_{u,v}(q⁻¹) is encoded as `Polynomial.reflect (ℓ v - ℓ u) (P u v)`, which equals X^n p(1/X) exactly when deg p ≤ n; this bound is guaranteed by the degree axiom (and P_{v,v}=1 with n=0).

Bruhat order `BruhatLE` is defined as the reflexive–transitive closure of x → x·t (t a reflection, ℓ(x) < ℓ(x t)), i.e. Björner–Brenti Definition 2.1.1. The exponent ℓ(w)−ℓ(y) uses natural subtraction, which is exact because y ≤ w implies ℓ(y) ≤ ℓ(w) (proved as API lemma `length_le_of_bruhatLE`).

'Complex semisimple Lie algebra' is modelled as `[LieAlgebra.IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]` (non-degenerate Killing form), which over ℂ is equivalent to finite-dimensional semisimple by Cartan's criterion; this is Mathlib's standard hypothesis for root systems of Lie algebras. The zero Lie algebra is allowed (statement is trivially true there).

The Weyl group is Mathlib's `RootPairing.weylGroup` of `LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H`, acting on weights `Dual ℂ H` via the automorphism action (checked by `rfl` that simple reflections act as μ ↦ μ − μ(α∨)α). Since Mathlib does not prove the Weyl group is finite or a Coxeter group, the theorems take `[Fintype W]` and a Coxeter system `cs` with hypothesis `hcs : ∀ i, cs.simple i = s_{α_i}` (simple reflections for the base b). Both hypotheses are always satisfiable (standard theorems), and length/Bruhat order/KL polynomials depend only on the generating set, so no vacuity or ambiguity arises.

The positive system is given by a base `b : RootPairing.Base` (Mathlib's notion, equivalent to the usual one for reduced root systems); positive roots are `b.IsPos`; ρ = (1/2)Σ_{α>0} α. The theorems quantify over all bases b; the article implicitly fixes one.

Verma module M(λ) is constructed genuinely as U(g)/I_λ where I_λ is the left ideal generated by ι(n⁺) (n⁺ = sum of positive root spaces) and ι(h) − λ(h)·1 for h ∈ H (Humphreys, Category O, §1.3). g acts through U(g) via `LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule` and `compLieHom`.

The simple quotient L(λ) is M(λ)/N(λ) with N(λ) := sSup of all proper Lie submodules, which is the unique maximal submodule by the standard theorem (if there were several maximal submodules the sSup would be ⊤; reviewer should note this relies on the standard fact, which holds).

Formal character `formalCharacter H X : Dual ℂ H → ℤ` is μ ↦ finrank of the weight space `LieModule.weightSpace X μ` (simultaneous eigenspaces for H, not generalised eigenspaces). Equality of characters is equality of these functions, matching ch(X) = Σ dim X_μ e^μ. All weight spaces of M_w and L_w are finite-dimensional so `finrank` never hits its junk value.
w₀ in part ii is any element with ∀ w, ℓ(w) ≤ ℓ(w₀) (unique in a finite Coxeter group), mirroring the article's 'element of maximal length'.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}$,
a choice of positive roots, Weyl vector $\rho$ (the half-sum of the positive roots) and finite Weyl
group $W$, regarded as a Coxeter group with the simple reflections as generators. For $w \in W$
let $M_w$ be the Verma module of highest weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$ and $L_w$ its irreducible
quotient, the simple highest weight module of highest weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$. Write
$\operatorname{ch}(X)$ for the formal character of a $\mathfrak{g}$-module $X$, i.e. the function
$\mu \mapsto \dim X_\mu$ on $\mathfrak{h}^*$, let $\ell$ be the Coxeter length, $\leq$ the Bruhat
order, $w_0$ the longest element of $W$ and $P_{y,w}(q)$ the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of $W$.
The two (equivalent) Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures, stated in the Inventiones paper of Kazhdan and
Lusztig (1979), are
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) = \sum_{y \leq w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} \, P_{y,w}(1)
  \operatorname{ch}(M_y)$$
and
$$\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \leq w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y).$$

They were proved independently by Beilinson–Bernstein and by Brylinski–Kashiwara in 1981.

Mathlib has Coxeter systems and the root system of a semisimple Lie algebra but neither the
Bruhat order, the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials nor Verma modules. These are introduced below.
The Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are pinned down by the properties that characterise them
uniquely (via the `R`-polynomials), and Verma modules and simple highest weight modules are
pinned down by their characterising properties (universal property, resp. irreducibility together
with a highest weight vector), so that the statements quantify over all modules with these
properties.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_polynomial%23Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_conjectures)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D. Kazhdan, G. Lusztig, *Representations of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras*,
  Invent. Math. 53 (1979), 165–184.
- A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein, *Localisation de 𝔤-modules*, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 292 (1981).
- J.-L. Brylinski, M. Kashiwara, *Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture and holonomic systems*,
  Invent. Math. 64 (1981), 387–410.
- A. Björner, F. Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter groups*, GTM 231, Springer (2005), Chapter 5.
-/

namespace KazhdanLusztigConjectures

open Polynomial

section Coxeter

variable {B W : Type*} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W)

local prefix:100 "ℓ" => cs.length
local prefix:100 "s" => cs.simple

/-- The Bruhat order of the Coxeter system `cs`: `BruhatLE cs u w` holds iff there is a chain
`u = x₀, x₁, …, xₖ = w` in `W` such that each `xⱼ₊₁ = xⱼ t` for a reflection `t` with
`ℓ(xⱼ) < ℓ(xⱼ₊₁)`. -/
def BruhatLE (u w : W) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun x y => ∃ t, cs.IsReflection t ∧ y = x * t ∧ ℓ x < ℓ y) u w

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma bruhatLE_refl (w : W) : BruhatLE cs w w :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma length_le_of_bruhatLE {u w : W} (h : BruhatLE cs u w) : ℓ u ≤ ℓ w := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact le_rfl
  | tail _ hstep ih =>
    obtain ⟨t, -, -, hlt⟩ := hstep
    exact ih.trans hlt.le

/-- `IsRPolynomialFamily cs R` says that `R : W → W → ℤ[q]` is the family of `R`-polynomials
`R_{x,y}` of Kazhdan and Lusztig for the Coxeter system `cs`. They are uniquely determined by
the recursion: `R_{x,y} = 0` unless `x ≤ y` in the Bruhat order, `R_{x,x} = 1`, and for a simple
reflection `s`:
* `R_{x,y} = R_{sx,sy}` if `sx < x` and `sy < y`;
* `R_{x,y} = R_{xs,ys}` if `xs < x` and `ys < y`;
* `R_{x,y} = (q - 1) R_{sx,y} + q R_{sx,sy}` if `sx > x` and `sy < y`.

Equivalently, in the Hecke algebra `T_{y⁻¹}⁻¹ = ∑ₓ R_{x,y}(q⁻¹) q^{-ℓ(x)} T_x`. -/
structure IsRPolynomialFamily (R : W → W → ℤ[X]) : Prop where
  eq_zero_of_not_bruhatLE (x y : W) : ¬ BruhatLE cs x y → R x y = 0
  self (x : W) : R x x = 1
  of_isLeftDescent (x y : W) (i : B) : cs.IsLeftDescent x i → cs.IsLeftDescent y i →
    R x y = R (s i * x) (s i * y)
  of_isRightDescent (x y : W) (i : B) : cs.IsRightDescent x i → cs.IsRightDescent y i →
    R x y = R (x * s i) (y * s i)
  of_not_isLeftDescent (x y : W) (i : B) : ¬ cs.IsLeftDescent x i → cs.IsLeftDescent y i →
    R x y = (X - 1) * R (s i * x) y + X * R (s i * x) (s i * y)

/-- `IsKazhdanLusztigFamily cs R P` says that `R` is the family of `R`-polynomials of `cs` and
that `P : W → W → ℤ[q]` is the family of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials `P_{y,w}` of `cs`. These are
uniquely determined by the following properties:
* `P_{y,w} = 0` unless `y ≤ w` in the Bruhat order;
* `P_{w,w} = 1`;
* `deg P_{y,w} ≤ (ℓ(w) - ℓ(y) - 1) / 2` for `y < w`;
* `q^{ℓ(w) - ℓ(y)} P_{y,w}(q⁻¹) = ∑_z R_{y,z}(q) P_{z,w}(q)` for all `y, w`.

The last identity is the invariance of `C'_w = q^{-ℓ(w)/2} ∑_{y ≤ w} P_{y,w} T_y` under the
involution of the Hecke algebra sending `q^{1/2}` to `q^{-1/2}` and `T_s` to `T_s⁻¹`. Here
`q^{ℓ(w) - ℓ(y)} P_{y,w}(q⁻¹)` is `Polynomial.reflect (ℓ w - ℓ y) (P y w)`, and only the terms
with `y ≤ z ≤ w` contribute to the sum. -/
structure IsKazhdanLusztigFamily (R P : W → W → ℤ[X]) : Prop where
  isRPolynomialFamily : IsRPolynomialFamily cs R
  eq_zero_of_not_bruhatLE (y w : W) : ¬ BruhatLE cs y w → P y w = 0
  self (w : W) : P w w = 1
  natDegree_le (y w : W) : BruhatLE cs y w → y ≠ w →
    (P y w).natDegree ≤ (ℓ w - ℓ y - 1) / 2
  reflect_eq (y w : W) : (P y w).reflect (ℓ w - ℓ y) = ∑ᶠ z, R y z * P z w

end Coxeter

section LieAlgebra

open LieAlgebra LieModule Module

variable {L : Type*} [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]
  {H : LieSubalgebra ℂ L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] (b : (IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Weyl vector `ρ ∈ 𝔥*`: half the sum of the roots that are positive with respect to the
base `b`. -/
noncomputable def weylVector : Dual ℂ H :=
  (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • ∑ α ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun α : H.root => b.IsPos α),
    ((α : Weight ℂ H L) : Dual ℂ H)

variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] [LieRingModule L V] [LieModule ℂ L V]

/-- A vector `v` of a `𝔤`-module `V` is *singular of weight `χ ∈ 𝔥*`* (with respect to the base
`b`) if `h ⬝ v = χ(h) v` for all `h ∈ 𝔥` and `x ⬝ v = 0` for all `x` in a positive root space.
Zero is allowed; a nonzero singular vector is a highest weight vector. -/
def IsSingularVector (χ : Dual ℂ H) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ h : H, ⁅(h : L), v⁆ = χ h • v) ∧
    ∀ α : H.root, b.IsPos α → ∀ x ∈ rootSpace H (α : Weight ℂ H L), ⁅x, v⁆ = 0

variable (V) in
/-- `IsVermaModule b χ V` says that the `𝔤`-module `V` is a Verma module of highest weight `χ`:
it contains a highest weight vector `v` of weight `χ` (nonzero singular vector) which is universal
in the sense that for every `𝔤`-module `N` and every singular vector `u ∈ N` of weight `χ` there
is a unique `𝔤`-module map `V → N` sending `v` to `u`. This is the universal property of
`M(χ) = U(𝔤) ⊗_{U(𝔟)} ℂ_χ`, so it characterises `M(χ)` up to isomorphism. -/
def IsVermaModule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, v ≠ 0 ∧ IsSingularVector b χ v ∧
    ∀ (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℂ N] [LieRingModule L N] [LieModule ℂ L N] (u : N),
      IsSingularVector b χ u → ∃! f : V →ₗ⁅ℂ,L⁆ N, f v = u

variable (V) in
/-- `IsSimpleHighestWeightModule b χ V` says that the `𝔤`-module `V` is the simple highest weight
module `L(χ)` of highest weight `χ`: it is irreducible and contains a highest weight vector of
weight `χ`. Such a module is the unique irreducible quotient of the Verma module `M(χ)`. -/
def IsSimpleHighestWeightModule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Prop :=
  IsIrreducible ℂ L V ∧ ∃ v : V, v ≠ 0 ∧ IsSingularVector b χ v

variable (V) in
/-- The formal character of a `𝔤`-module `V`, as a function on `𝔥*`: `μ ↦ dim V_μ`, where `V_μ`
is the `μ`-weight space of `V` for the Cartan subalgebra `𝔥`. -/
noncomputable def formalCharacter (μ : Dual ℂ H) : ℕ :=
  finrank ℂ (weightSpace V (μ : H → ℂ))

local notation "W" => RootPairing.weylGroup (IsKilling.rootSystem H)
local notation "ρ" => weylVector b

variable {M : CoxeterMatrix b.support} (cs : CoxeterSystem M (IsKilling.rootSystem H).weylGroup)

local prefix:100 "ℓ" => cs.length

/-- **The first Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture.**

Let `𝔤` be a complex semisimple Lie algebra (a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra with
non-degenerate Killing form) with Cartan subalgebra `𝔥`, and fix a base `b` of the root system,
i.e. a choice of positive roots. Let `W` be the Weyl group, viewed as a Coxeter group `cs` whose
simple reflections are the reflections in the simple roots (`hcs`), with length `ℓ` and Bruhat
order `≤`, and let `P_{y,w}` be its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Let `ρ` be the half-sum of the
positive roots. For `w ∈ W` let `L_w` be the simple highest weight module of highest weight
`-w(ρ) - ρ`, and for `y ∈ W` let `M_y` be the Verma module of highest weight `-y(ρ) - ρ`. Then
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) = \sum_{y \leq w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} \, P_{y,w}(1)
  \operatorname{ch}(M_y),$$
i.e. for every `μ ∈ 𝔥*`, `dim (L_w)_μ = ∑_{y ≤ w} (-1)^{ℓ(w) - ℓ(y)} P_{y,w}(1) dim (M_y)_μ`.

Proved by Beilinson–Bernstein and by Brylinski–Kashiwara (1981). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20 22]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i

For reduced root systems (the Lie algebra case) Mathlib's `Base` coincides with the usual notion. The statements quantify over every Cartan subalgebra `H` and every base `b` (all choices are conjugate).

The Weyl group is Mathlib's `(rootSystem H).weylGroup` (subgroup of root-pairing automorphisms generated by reflections), acting on `𝔥* = Dual ℂ H` by `•`. Bruhat order `BruhatLE cs` is defined as the reflexive-transitive closure of `x → x t` for reflections `t` with `ℓ(x) < ℓ(x t)` (Björner–Brenti Def. 2.1.1). An API lemma proves `y ≤ w → ℓ y ≤ ℓ w`, so the natural-number subtraction in `(-1)^(ℓ w - ℓ y)` is the true difference on the summation range.

Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are not constructed via the Hecke algebra; instead the theorems quantify over any families `R P : W → W → ℤ[X]` satisfying `IsKazhdanLusztigFamily cs R P`, the standard uniqueness characterisation (Björner–Brenti Thm 5.1.1 and 5.1.4 / Humphreys §7.5, 7.9–7.11): R satisfies Wikipedia's recursion (vanishing unless x ≤ y, R_{x,x}=1, the left/right descent cases and `(q-1)R_{sx,y} + qR_{sx,sy}`), and P satisfies P_{y,w}=0 unless y ≤ w, P_{w,w}=1, natDegree ≤ (ℓ(w)-ℓ(y)-1)/2 for y<w, and `q^{ℓ(w)-ℓ(y)} P_{y,w}(q⁻¹) = ∑_z R_{y,z} P_{z,w}` (encoded with `Polynomial.reflect (ℓ w - ℓ y)`, valid because of the degree bound; sum over all z via `finsum`, only y ≤ z ≤ w contribute). Existence of such families is the Kazhdan–Lusztig theorem; uniqueness follows by induction. Reviewer should check these conditions (I verified them by hand on A1, A2 and the A3 example P_{b,bacb}=1+q).

Verma module `M(χ)` is characterised by its universal property (`IsVermaModule`): a nonzero singular vector `v` of weight `χ` (H-weight vector killed by all positive root spaces `rootSpace H α`, `b.IsPos α`) such that for every 𝔤-module `N` (in a fixed but arbitrary universe) and every singular vector `u ∈ N` of weight `χ` there is a unique Lie module map `V → N` with `v ↦ u`. This is Frobenius reciprocity for `U(𝔤) ⊗_{U(𝔟)} ℂ_χ` and determines `M(χ)` up to isomorphism.

The simple module `L(χ)` is characterised (`IsSimpleHighestWeightModule`) as an irreducible 𝔤-module (`LieModule.IsIrreducible`) containing a nonzero singular vector of weight `χ`; any such module is the unique simple quotient of `M(χ)`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures

The Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures relate the values at $q = 1$ of the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
$P_{y,w}(q)$ of a finite Weyl group $W$ to the representation theory of the corresponding complex
semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Let $\rho$ be the half-sum of the positive roots. For
$w \in W$ let $M_w$ be the Verma module of highest weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$ and let $L_w$ be its
simple quotient. Writing $\operatorname{ch}$ for the formal character, the conjectures state
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) = \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1)
  \operatorname{ch}(M_y),
\qquad
\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y),$$
where $\le$ is the Bruhat order, $\ell$ the Coxeter length and $w_0$ the longest element of $W$.
Both were proved in 1981 by Beilinson–Bernstein and by Brylinski–Kashiwara.

Mathlib has neither Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials nor Verma modules. This file therefore defines
the Bruhat order, the $R$-polynomials and the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of an arbitrary Coxeter
system (following Björner–Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter groups*, Theorems 5.1.1 and 5.1.4),
and characterises Verma modules by their universal property and simple highest weight modules by
irreducibility. Since Mathlib does not yet know that a Weyl group is a Coxeter group, the
statements take as a hypothesis a Coxeter system on the Weyl group whose simple reflections are
the reflections in the simple roots; such a Coxeter system exists and is unique.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_polynomial%23Kazhdan%E2%80%93Lusztig_conjectures)
* D. Kazhdan, G. Lusztig, *Representations of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras*,
  Invent. Math. 53 (1979), 165–184.
* A. Björner, F. Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter groups*, GTM 231, Springer, 2005, Chapter 5.
* J. E. Humphreys, *Representations of semisimple Lie algebras in the BGG category 𝒪*,
  GSM 94, AMS, 2008, Chapter 8.
-/

universe u

open LieAlgebra LieModule Module Polynomial

namespace KazhdanLusztigConjectures

/- ### Bruhat order and Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of a Coxeter system -/

section Coxeter

variable {B W : Type*} [Group W] {cm : CoxeterMatrix B} (cs : CoxeterSystem cm W)

/-- The Bruhat order of the Coxeter system `cs`: `u ≤ w` if and only if there are reflections
$t_1, \dots, t_k$ with $w = u t_1 \cdots t_k$ and
$\ell(u t_1 \cdots t_{i-1}) < \ell(u t_1 \cdots t_i)$ for all $i$. -/
def BruhatLE (u w : W) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen
    (fun x y ↦ ∃ t, cs.IsReflection t ∧ y = x * t ∧ cs.length x < cs.length y) u w

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem bruhatLE_refl (w : W) : BruhatLE cs w w :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem BruhatLE.trans {u v w : W} (huv : BruhatLE cs u v) (hvw : BruhatLE cs v w) :
    BruhatLE cs u w :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.trans huv hvw

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem bruhatLE_one_simple (i : B) : BruhatLE cs 1 (cs.simple i) :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.single ⟨cs.simple i, cs.isReflection_simple i, by simp, by simp⟩

open scoped Classical in
/-- The $R$-polynomials $R_{x,w}(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q]$ of the Coxeter system `cs`, defined by
recursion on $\ell(w)$: $R_{x,1} = \delta_{x,1}$ and, if $w \ne 1$ and $s$ is a right descent of
$w$ (that is $\ell(ws) < \ell(w)$), then
$$R_{x,w} = \begin{cases} R_{xs,ws} & \text{if } \ell(xs) < \ell(x), \\
q\,R_{xs,ws} + (q - 1)\,R_{x,ws} & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
The result does not depend on the choice of the right descent $s$
(Björner–Brenti, Theorem 5.1.1), so we may pick one arbitrarily. -/
noncomputable def rPolynomial : W → W → ℤ[X]
  | x, w =>
    if hw : w = 1 then (if x = 1 then 1 else 0)
    else
      if cs.length (x * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose) < cs.length x then
        rPolynomial (x * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose)
          (w * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose)
      else
        X * rPolynomial (x * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose)
          (w * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose) +
        (X - 1) * rPolynomial x (w * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose)
termination_by _ w => cs.length w
decreasing_by all_goals exact (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hw).choose_spec

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem rPolynomial_one_one : rPolynomial cs 1 1 = 1 := by
  rw [rPolynomial]
  simp

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem rPolynomial_eq_zero_of_ne_one {x : W} (hx : x ≠ 1) : rPolynomial cs x 1 = 0 := by
  rw [rPolynomial]
  simp [hx]

/-- $R_{1,s} = q - 1$ for every simple reflection $s$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem rPolynomial_one_simple (i : B) : rPolynomial cs 1 (cs.simple i) = X - 1 := by
  have hne : cs.simple i ≠ 1 := by
    intro h
    simpa [h] using cs.length_simple i
  have hjd : cs.length (cs.simple i * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hne).choose) <
      cs.length (cs.simple i) := (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hne).choose_spec
  have h1 : cs.simple i * cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hne).choose = 1 := by
    have := cs.length_simple i
    exact cs.length_eq_zero_iff.mp (by omega)
  have hne' : cs.simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hne).choose ≠ 1 := by
    intro h
    simpa [h] using cs.length_simple (cs.exists_rightDescent_of_ne_one hne).choose
  rw [rPolynomial, dif_neg hne, one_mul, h1, cs.length_simple, cs.length_one,
    if_neg (by omega), rPolynomial_one_one, rPolynomial_eq_zero_of_ne_one cs hne']
  ring

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,w}(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q]$ of the Coxeter system `cs`.

They are the unique polynomials with $P_{w,w} = 1$, $P_{x,w} = 0$ unless $x \le w$ in the Bruhat
order, $\deg P_{x,w} \le (\ell(w) - \ell(x) - 1)/2$ for $x < w$, and
$$q^{\ell(w) - \ell(x)} P_{x,w}(q^{-1}) = \sum_{x \le y \le w} R_{x,y}(q)\, P_{y,w}(q)$$
(Björner–Brenti, Theorem 5.1.4). Since $R_{x,y} = 0$ unless $x \le y$, the terms with $y \ne x$
of the right hand side are exactly the terms with $\ell(x) < \ell(y)$, and the degree bound forces
$P_{x,w}$ to be the negative of the part of degree $< (\ell(w) - \ell(x) + 1)/2$ of
$\sum_{\ell(x) < \ell(y)} R_{x,y} P_{y,w}$. This is the recursion used here; it is well founded in
$\ell(w) - \ell(x)$. -/
noncomputable def klPolynomial : W → W → ℤ[X]
  | x, w =>
    if x = w then 1

    intro h

/- ### Highest weight modules of a complex semisimple Lie algebra -/

section LieAlgebra

/- `L` is a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form (that is, a
complex semisimple Lie algebra), `H` is a Cartan subalgebra and `b` is a base (system of simple
roots) of the root system of `L` relative to `H`. -/
variable {L : Type*} [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]
  (H : LieSubalgebra ℂ L) [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] (b : (IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Weyl vector $\rho \in \mathfrak h^*$: the half-sum of the positive roots relative to `b`. -/
noncomputable def weylVector : Dual ℂ H :=
  (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ∑ α : H.root with b.IsPos α, (IsKilling.rootSystem H).root α

variable {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℂ M] [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule ℂ L M]

/-- A vector `v` of an `L`-module is *primitive of weight `χ`* if every `h ∈ H` acts on `v` by
`χ h` and every root vector for a positive root (relative to `b`) annihilates `v`. -/
def IsPrimitiveVector (v : M) (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Prop :=
  (∀ h : H, ⁅(h : L), v⁆ = χ h • v) ∧
    ∀ α : H.root, b.IsPos α → ∀ x ∈ rootSpace H (α : Weight ℂ H L), ⁅x, v⁆ = 0

variable (M) in
/-- `M` is a *Verma module of highest weight `χ`*: it is generated by a nonzero primitive vector
`v` of weight `χ`, and for every `L`-module `N` and every primitive vector `u ∈ N` of weight `χ`
there is a homomorphism of `L`-modules `M → N` sending `v` to `u`. This is the universal
property of $M(\chi) = U(\mathfrak g) \otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)} \mathbb C_\chi$ and characterises
it up to isomorphism. -/
def IsVermaModule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Prop :=
  ∃ v : M, v ≠ 0 ∧ IsPrimitiveVector H b v χ ∧ LieSubmodule.lieSpan ℂ L {v} = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℂ N] [LieRingModule L N] [LieModule ℂ L N]
      (u : N), IsPrimitiveVector H b u χ → ∃ f : M →ₗ⁅ℂ,L⁆ N, f v = u

variable (M) in
/-- `M` is a *simple highest weight module of highest weight `χ`*: it is an irreducible
`L`-module containing a nonzero primitive vector of weight `χ`. Such a module is isomorphic to
the unique simple quotient $L(\chi)$ of the Verma module $M(\chi)$. -/
def IsSimpleHighestWeightModule (χ : Dual ℂ H) : Prop :=
  IsIrreducible ℂ L M ∧ ∃ v : M, v ≠ 0 ∧ IsPrimitiveVector H b v χ

variable (M) in
/-- The formal character of the `L`-module `M`: the function $\mu \mapsto \dim M_\mu$ on
$\mathfrak h^*$, where $M_\mu$ is the `μ`-weight space of `M` for the action of `H`. -/
noncomputable def formalCharacter (μ : Dual ℂ H) : ℕ :=
  finrank ℂ (weightSpace M (μ : H → ℂ))

end LieAlgebra

/- ### The conjectures -/

section Conjectures

variable {L : Type*} [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]
  (H : LieSubalgebra ℂ L) [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] (b : (IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base)

local notation "W" => RootPairing.weylGroup (IsKilling.rootSystem H)
local notation "ρ" => weylVector H b

/-- **First Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein
and by Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981).

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a
choice of simple roots, Weyl group $W$ and Weyl vector $\rho$ (the half-sum of the positive
roots). The simple reflections make $W$ a Coxeter group; let $\ell$ be its length function,
$\le$ its Bruhat order and $P_{y,w}$ its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. For $w \in W$ let $M_w$ be
the Verma module of highest weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$ and $L_w$ the simple module of highest
weight $-w(\rho) - \rho$. Then, for every $w \in W$,
$$\operatorname{ch}(L_w) = \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1)
  \operatorname{ch}(M_y),$$
as an identity of formal characters, i.e. for every $\mu \in \mathfrak h^*$,
$\dim (L_w)_\mu = \sum_{y \le w} (-1)^{\ell(w) - \ell(y)} P_{y,w}(1) \dim (M_y)_\mu$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i
    (cm : CoxeterMatrix b.support) (cs : CoxeterSystem cm W)
    (hcs : ∀ i : b.support, cs.simple i = RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx (IsKilling.rootSystem H) i)
    (w : W)
    (Lw : Type u) [AddCommGroup Lw] [Module ℂ Lw] [LieRingModule L Lw] [LieModule ℂ L Lw]
    (hLw : IsSimpleHighestWeightModule H b Lw (-(w • ρ) - ρ))
    (M : W → Type u) [∀ y, AddCommGroup (M y)] [∀ y, Module ℂ (M y)]
    [∀ y, LieRingModule L (M y)] [∀ y, LieModule ℂ L (M y)]
    (hM : ∀ y, IsVermaModule H b (M y) (-(y • ρ) - ρ)) (μ : Dual ℂ H) :
    (formalCharacter H Lw μ : ℤ) =
      ∑ᶠ (y) (_ : BruhatLE cs y w),
        (-1) ^ (cs.length w - cs.length y) * (klPolynomial cs y w).eval 1 *
          (formalCharacter H (M y) μ : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/-- **Second Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture** (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979; proved by Beilinson–Bernstein
and by Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981). It is equivalent to the first one.

With notation as in `kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.i` and $w_0$ the longest element of $W$,
for every $w \in W$,
$$\operatorname{ch}(M_w) = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \operatorname{ch}(L_y),$$
as an identity of formal characters, i.e. for every $\mu \in \mathfrak h^*$,
$\dim (M_w)_\mu = \sum_{y \le w} P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1) \dim (L_y)_\mu$. Equivalently, the
Jordan–Hölder multiplicity of $L_y$ in $M_w$ is $P_{w_0 w, w_0 y}(1)$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 17 20]
theorem kazhdan_lusztig_conjectures.parts.ii
    (cm : CoxeterMatrix b.support) (cs : CoxeterSystem cm W)
    (hcs : ∀ i : b.support, cs.simple i = RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx (IsKilling.rootSystem H) i)
    (w₀ : W) (hw₀ : ∀ v : W, cs.length v ≤ cs.length w₀) (w : W)
    (Mw : Type u) [AddCommGroup Mw] [Module ℂ Mw] [LieRingModule L Mw] [LieModule ℂ L Mw]
    (hMw : IsVermaModule H b Mw (-(w • ρ) - ρ))
    (Lmod : W → Type u) [∀ y, AddCommGroup (Lmod y)] [∀ y, Module ℂ (Lmod y)]
    [∀ y, LieRingModule L (Lmod y)] [∀ y, LieModule ℂ L (Lmod y)]
    (hLmod : ∀ y, IsSimpleHighestWeightModule H b (Lmod y) (-(y • ρ) - ρ)) (μ : Dual ℂ H) :
    (formalCharacter H Mw μ : ℤ) =
      ∑ᶠ (y) (_ : BruhatLE cs y w),
        (klPolynomial cs (w₀ * w) (w₀ * y)).eval 1 * (formalCharacter H (Lmod y) μ : ℤ) := by
  sorry

end Conjectures

end KazhdanLusztigConjectures

The problem header lists the status as 'open' while the table notes (correctly) say both parts are theorems since 1981 and should be `research solved`; I followed the table notes and the repository's category rules and tagged both `research solved`.
modeling_decisions: Category: both slots are tagged `research solved` (Beilinson–Bernstein and Brylinski–Kashiwara, 1981), following the decomposition-table notes and CONTRIBUTING.md, even though the Wikipedia list entry (and the problem header) says 'open'.

'Complex semisimple Lie algebra' is rendered as `[LieRing L] [LieAlgebra ℂ L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling ℂ L] [FiniteDimensional ℂ L]` (non-degenerate Killing form). Over a field of characteristic zero this is equivalent to semisimplicity, and it is what Mathlib's root-system API (`LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem`) requires; Mathlib does not have the converse instance semisimple → IsKilling.

The Weyl group is `RootPairing.weylGroup (IsKilling.rootSystem H)` (a subgroup of root-pairing automorphisms) acting on h^* = `Module.Dual ℂ H` through the built-in action; I verified that `weylGroup.ofIdx i • χ = χ - χ(α_i^∨) α_i`, the standard reflection. Highest weights are `-(w • ρ) - ρ` with ρ = `weylVector H b`, the half-sum of the roots that are positive for the base `b` (`b.IsPos`).

Mathlib does not know that a Weyl group with its simple reflections is a Coxeter group, so both theorems quantify over a Coxeter matrix `cm : CoxeterMatrix b.support` and a Coxeter system `cs : CoxeterSystem cm W` with the hypothesis `hcs : ∀ i, cs.simple i = weylGroup.ofIdx (rootSystem H) i`. Such a `cs` exists and is unique, and length, Bruhat order and KL polynomials depend only on the set of simple reflections, so the hypothesis is non-vacuous and pins down the intended structures.
Bruhat order `BruhatLE cs` is defined for any Coxeter system as the reflexive–transitive closure of u → u·t with t a reflection (`cs.IsReflection`) and ℓ(u) < ℓ(u t) (Björner–Brenti Def. 2.1.1).

R-polynomials `rPolynomial cs` are defined by the standard recursion on ℓ(w) (Björner–Brenti Thm 5.1.1) using a right descent chosen with `Classical.choose`; the recursion is independent of this choice by the uniqueness part of that theorem (proof by induction on ℓ(w)). The reviewer should check this recursion against the source; the file includes the test `R_{1,s} = q - 1`.

KL polynomials `klPolynomial cs` are defined by well-founded recursion on ℓ(w)-ℓ(x) from the characterisation q^{ℓ(w)-ℓ(x)} P_{x,w}(q⁻¹) = Σ_{x≤y≤w} R_{x,y} P_{y,w} plus the degree bound deg P_{x,w} ≤ (ℓ(w)-ℓ(x)-1)/2 (Björner–Brenti Thm 5.1.4; this is equivalent to the Hecke-algebra definition given in the Wikipedia article): P_{x,w} is minus the part of degree < (ℓ(w)-ℓ(x)+1)/2 of Σ_{ℓ(x)<ℓ(y)} R_{x,y} P_{y,w}. The sum is over all y with ℓ(x)<ℓ(y) (rather than x<y≤w) purely for termination; extra terms vanish because R_{x,y}=0 unless x≤y and P_{y,w}=0 unless y≤w. Tests `P_{w,w}=1`, `P_{x,w}=0` when ℓ(w)≤ℓ(x), x≠w, and `P_{1,s}=1` are proved in the file.

The Verma module M(χ) is characterised (`IsVermaModule`) by: a nonzero primitive vector v of weight χ (h acts by χ(h), positive root spaces kill v) generating M as a Lie submodule, together with the universal property that every primitive vector u of weight χ in any L-module N (in the same universe as M) is the image of v under some L-module homomorphism M → N. This is Hom_g(M(χ),N) ≅ Hom_b(ℂ_χ,N) and determines M up to isomorphism. The simple module L(χ) is characterised (`IsSimpleHighestWeightModule`) as an irreducible L-module (`LieModule.IsIrreducible`) with a nonzero primitive vector of weight χ.

Formal characters are compared pointwise: `formalCharacter H M μ = finrank ℂ (weightSpace M μ)` (weight spaces for the action of H), and the conjectures are stated as ∀ μ : Dual ℂ H, cast to ℤ. All weight spaces of Verma modules and their quotients are finite dimensional, so `finrank` is the honest dimension.

Since Mathlib has no `Finite` instance for the Weyl group of a finite root system, sums over {y ≤ w} are written with `finsum` (`∑ᶠ (y) (_ : BruhatLE cs y w), …`), which equals the finite sum because W is finite. The sign is `(-1 : ℤ) ^ (cs.length w - cs.length y)` with natural subtraction, harmless because y ≤ w implies ℓ(y) ≤ ℓ(w).
The longest element w₀ in part ii is taken as any `w₀` with `∀ v, cs.length v ≤ cs.length w₀` (it exists and is unique for a finite Coxeter group).

Families of modules: since the sums range over y, part i quantifies over a family `M : W → Type u` of Verma modules (with `hM : ∀ y, IsVermaModule …`) and part ii over a family of simple modules; because any two Verma (resp. simple highest weight) modules of the same weight are isomorphic, the statements do not depend on the choice.
